goal: Detect a stalled or dropped Slack Socket Mode connection in the kranz serve --slack bridge, reconnect automatically with backoff, and expose an observable liveness signal so a dead bridge is loud rather than silent.

validationContract.statement: When the Socket Mode connection receives no frames for the idle-timeout window, the pump loop ends the connection with the reconnect outcome instead of blocking forever.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-slack idle_timeout 2>&1 | grep -qE 'idle_timeout_triggers_reconnect \.\.\. ok'

validationContract.statement: A Slack 'disconnect' frame ends the current connection with the reconnect outcome (the bridge pre-empts Slack's teardown rather than ignoring the warning).
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-slack disconnect_frame 2>&1 | grep -qE 'disconnect_frame_triggers_reconnect \.\.\. ok'

validationContract.statement: The bridge liveness snapshot reports 'stale' once the time since the last received frame exceeds the staleness threshold.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-slack health_reports_stale 2>&1 | grep -qE 'health_reports_stale_after_threshold \.\.\. ok'

validationContract.statement: The bridge liveness snapshot reports 'live' when a frame was received within the staleness threshold.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-slack health_reports_live 2>&1 | grep -qE 'health_reports_live_within_threshold \.\.\. ok'

validationContract.statement: The full kranz-slack test suite (existing inbound/outbound/ack/dedup behavior plus the new tests) compiles and passes — no regression in the socket loop's production behavior.

While running, the bridge emits a periodic health log line reflecting connection state and time-since-last-frame, and logs a distinct loud (warn-level) line when a stall is detected or a reconnect occurs — so an operator watching logs sees a dead bridge.

milestones.title: A stalled or Slack-warned socket auto-reconnects

features.title: Harden the Socket Mode pump loop: injectable test seam, idle-timeout stall detection, and disconnect-frame reconnect
features.spec:
CONTEXT: In crates/slack/src/bridge.rs, `run_socket` reconnects with capped exponential backoff (BACKOFF_MIN/BACKOFF_MAX), but only when `connect_once` RETURNS. `connect_once` runs an inner `loop { tokio::select! { _ = stop.notified() => ...; msg = read.next() => match msg { ... } } }` over a split tokio-tungstenite websocket. It returns Ok(true) on shutdown, Ok(false) on a clean Close/None or write-send failure (caller reconnects, resetting backoff), and Err on a stream error (caller reconnects, growing backoff). TWO real bugs: (1) `read.next()` has NO timeout — if the TCP connection dies silently (no FIN/RST, as happens after a long idle period following a sibling drain) the select parks forever, `connect_once` never returns, and the existing reconnect machinery is never reached — this is the live silent-failure symptom. (2) Slack sends a `{"type":"disconnect", "reason":"warning"|"refresh_requested"}` frame before tearing a socket down; today `route()` classifies it as Action::Ignore (see crates/slack/src/inbound.rs around line 308 and the test at ~2136) and it carries no envelope_id, so the loop silently drops it and keeps pumping a doomed socket.

TASK:
1. Refactor the inner read/select loop OUT of `connect_once` into a separate async function (e.g. `pump_connection`) that is generic over the read stream and write sink so it can be driven by an in-memory stream in tests instead of a live websocket. Suggested signature shape: generic `R: futures_util::Stream<Item = Result<tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Message, E>> + Unpin` and `W: futures_util::Sink<tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Message> + Unpin`, plus the same `stop: &Arc<Notify>`, `SeenEnvelopes`, and dispatch dependencies it uses today. `connect_once` keeps opening the wss URL (client.open_connection + connect_async) and calls the new function with the real split halves. PRESERVE production behavior EXACTLY: ack-first (send `{"envelope_id":id}` before slow work), SeenEnvelopes dedup, `is_slow_action` spawn-off-the-read-loop, Ping->Pong, and the same Ok(true)/Ok(false)/Err return contract.
2. Add an idle timeout. Introduce `const IDLE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(45);`. Wrap the `read.next()` await in `tokio::time::timeout(IDLE_TIMEOUT, ...)`; when it elapses, log a loud `tracing::warn!` (e.g. "slack socket idle N s; treating as stalled, reconnecting") and return `Ok(false)` so the existing caller reconnects. Normal Slack traffic (pings every few seconds) keeps this from firing in a healthy session.
3. Handle the disconnect frame. Add a small pure helper `fn is_disconnect_frame(text: &str) -> bool` that returns true when the frame parses to JSON with top-level `type == "disconnect"`. In the pump loop, on a Text frame, check this FIRST; if true, log at info/warn and return `Ok(false)` (reconnect) — do not route it. Unit-test the helper directly too.
4. TESTS (in #[cfg(test)] within bridge.rs or a tests/ file). Use `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance()` and an in-memory stream (e.g. a `futures_util` stream built from a channel or `stream::pending()`/`stream::iter`) plus a sink that collects sent messages (e.g. `Vec`-backed or `futures_util::sink::drain()`), so no live Slack is needed. Required test names (the mission contract greps for these EXACT names):
   - `idle_timeout_triggers_reconnect`: drive `pump_connection` with a read stream that never yields another frame; advance virtual time past IDLE_TIMEOUT; assert the function returns `Ok(false)`.
   - `disconnect_frame_triggers_reconnect`: feed a single `{"type":"disconnect","reason":"refresh_requested"}` Text frame; assert the function returns `Ok(false)` and did NOT dispatch it as an action.
   Keep/adjust any existing tests that referenced the old inline loop shape.
5. Run `cargo fmt` before finishing (this repo has previously lost a full respawn to an unformatted worker diff), then `cargo clippy -p kranz-slack` and `cargo test -p kranz-slack` and confirm green.

CONSTRAINTS: Do not touch crates/server or crates/cli. Do not change the outbound loop (`run_bridge`). Keep the tungstenite Message import path stable. The idle timeout must be a named constant, not a magic literal.
validationCriteria: A test named `idle_timeout_triggers_reconnect` drives the extracted pump function with a stream that yields no frames, advances virtual time past IDLE_TIMEOUT via tokio::time, and asserts the function returns Ok(false); the per-test line `idle_timeout_triggers_reconnect ... ok` appears in `cargo test -p kranz-slack` output.

A test named `disconnect_frame_triggers_reconnect` feeds a {"type":"disconnect"} Text frame and asserts the pump function returns Ok(false) without dispatching it; the per-test line `disconnect_frame_triggers_reconnect ... ok` appears.
`is_disconnect_frame` is a pure helper unit-tested for a disconnect frame (true) and a non-disconnect frame such as a slash_commands envelope (false).
`cargo test -p kranz-slack` prints `result: ok` (full suite, including all pre-existing inbound/outbound/ack/dedup tests, still passes) and the diff is `cargo fmt`-clean.
Production ack-first ordering, SeenEnvelopes dedup, is_slow_action spawn behavior, and Ping->Pong handling are preserved (unchanged externally observable behavior).

features.title: Shared bridge liveness state with periodic health log and loud stall/reconnect logging
features.spec:
CONTEXT: This builds directly on Milestone 1's refactored pump loop in crates/slack/src/bridge.rs (the `pump_connection` function and `run_socket`/`connect_once`). Milestone 1 is complete and validated before this feature runs. Goal: make a stalled/dead bridge observable through logs, since today there is no liveness signal anywhere (the server's /api/health knows nothing about the bridge, and there is no last-frame timestamp or periodic log).

TASK:
1. Add a shared liveness handle, e.g. `#[derive(Clone)] struct BridgeHealth(Arc<Mutex<HealthState>>)` (or an atomics-based equivalent) holding at least: `connected: bool`, `last_frame_at: Option<Instant>`, and a monotonically increasing `connect_count`. Consider a small `health` module or keep it in bridge.rs.
2. Provide mutation methods used by the loop: `record_connected()` (set connected=true, bump connect_count, stamp last_frame_at=now), `record_frame()` (stamp last_frame_at=now), `record_disconnected()` (connected=false). Wire these into the code paths from Milestone 1: call record_connected when connect_once establishes the socket, record_frame on EVERY received frame inside pump_connection, and record_disconnected when a connection ends (stall, disconnect frame, close, or error).
3. Make the staleness decision PURE and testable independent of the wall clock: e.g. `fn snapshot(&self, now: Instant) -> HealthSnapshot` returning `{ connected: bool, secs_since_frame: Option<u64>, stale: bool }`, where `stale` is true iff `now - last_frame_at > STALENESS_THRESHOLD` (`const STALENESS_THRESHOLD: Duration`; pick a value >= the M1 idle timeout, e.g. 60s). The threshold comparison must be computed from the two Instants/Durations passed in — do NOT call Instant::now() inside the pure computation, so tests pass explicit values.
4. Add a periodic health-log task in `run_socket`: a `tokio::time::interval` (e.g. `const HEALTH_LOG_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);`) that, each tick, reads the snapshot and logs it — `tracing::info!` when connected and not stale (e.g. "slack bridge healthy: connected, last frame Ns ago"), and `tracing::warn!` when disconnected OR stale (e.g. "slack bridge UNHEALTHY: no frame in Ns"). This task must also stop on the shared shutdown notify, like the other loops.
5. Ensure loud logging on the transition events: a `tracing::info!` on (re)connect and a `tracing::warn!` on stall-detected and on reconnect-after-drop (some of this may already exist from M1 — make sure the stall and reconnect cases are warn-level and clearly worded).
6. TESTS over the pure snapshot logic (contract greps for these EXACT names):
   - `health_reports_stale_after_threshold`: build a HealthState whose last_frame_at is `now - (STALENESS_THRESHOLD + 1s)`; assert `snapshot(now).stale == true`.
   - `health_reports_live_within_threshold`: last_frame_at is `now - (STALENESS_THRESHOLD / 2)`; assert `snapshot(now).stale == false` and `connected == true`.
   Construct the Instants in-test via `Instant::now()` +/- Duration arithmetic passed into the pure fn (no reliance on real elapsed time / no sleeps).
7. Run `cargo fmt`, then `cargo clippy -p kranz-slack` and `cargo test -p kranz-slack`; confirm green.

CONSTRAINTS: Stay entirely within crates/slack — do NOT add a server route or touch crates/server or crates/cli (the HTTP /api/slack/health endpoint is explicitly out of scope for this mission). Do not spam the Slack channel; the health signal is log-based only. All thresholds/intervals are named constants.
validationCriteria: A `BridgeHealth` shared handle records last-frame time on every received frame, connected on socket establishment, and disconnected when a connection ends, and these calls are wired into the Milestone 1 pump loop / connect paths.

A test named `health_reports_stale_after_threshold` asserts the pure snapshot reports stale==true when the last frame is older than STALENESS_THRESHOLD; the per-test line `health_reports_stale_after_threshold ... ok` appears in `cargo test -p kranz-slack`.

A test named `health_reports_live_within_threshold` asserts the pure snapshot reports stale==false and connected==true when a frame arrived within the threshold; the per-test line `health_reports_live_within_threshold ... ok` appears.
`run_socket` spawns a periodic (interval-based) task that logs the health snapshot at info when healthy and at warn when disconnected or stale, and stops on the shared shutdown notify.
Stall detection and reconnect events are logged at warn level with clear wording; a (re)connect logs at info; the change is `cargo fmt`-clean and `cargo test -p kranz-slack` prints `result: ok`.
